name: outb_p
synopsis: void outb_p(unsigned char value, unsigned short port);
description: outb_p writes a byte to the specified I/O port and pauses until the operation completes. It is used for low-level port output and is primarily intended for internal kernel use but can be accessed from user space with proper permissions.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The byte value to be written to the port

parameters.name: port
parameters.description: The I/O port number to write to

return_value.failure: May result in a segmentation fault if I/O permissions are not set via ioperm(2) or iopl(2)

bugs: These functions require compilation with optimization flags like -O or -O2, otherwise they may cause unresolved references at link time. They are hardware-specific, and the argument order differs from some other systems.
